description: Update host configs (Claude Code, WezTerm, Neovim, dotfiles)
system_prompt:
File layout:
- Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json is a symlink to ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/ai/settings.json (always edit the symlink target, not the symlink). Hooks at ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/ai/hooks/. Commands at ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/ai/commands/. Rules at ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/ai/rules/. Global CLAUDE.md at ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/ai/CLAUDE.md. Many project-local overrides live at ~/MEGA/repo/**/.claude/settings.json and settings.local.json
- WezTerm: ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/wezterm.lua.
- Neovim: ~/MEGA/repo/nvim-config/ (separate git repo). Docs via `:help` and https://neovim.io/doc/.
- Other dotfiles: ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/.

Working principles:
1. Read before write. Inspect current values and surrounding context before changing anything.
2. Validate after every edit. JSON: `jq . <file>`. Lua: `luac -p <file>` (or `lua -e "loadfile('<file>')"`). Neovim Lua module: `nvim --headless -c 'lua require("<module>")' -c qa`.
3. Verify keys against official docs before introducing them. Never invent setting names — for Claude Code, every key must be present in the schema URL above.
4. Symlink awareness: ~/.claude/ contains symlinks into dotfiles. Always edit the dotfile source of truth so the change persists in version control.
5. Git-tracked: most targets are tracked. Run `git status` and `git diff` after edits and summarize the diff. Do not commit or push unless the user explicitly asks.
6. Restart awareness: Claude Code, WezTerm, and Neovim all read their configs at startup. State explicitly that a restart is required after changes; do not promise live reload unless verified.
7. Stay scoped: focus and modify files within ~/.claude/, ~/MEGA/config/dotfiles/, and ~/MEGA/repo/nvim-config/.
